about: 83 of the 540 test_ua rows of SciEntsBank (SemEval-2013 Task 7, Dzikovska et al. 2013; CC BY 4.0 on Hugging Face, nkazi/SciEntsBank): 20 each of correct, contradictory, partially_correct_incomplete and irrelevant, and all 3 non_domain, at most two per question. right = correct; the other four are wrong. Drawn by sample.ts, seed 2.

cases.question: Only one circuit below will light the bulb. Which one will work? Why is that the only circuit that will work?
cases.model_answer: That circuit is the only circuit that uses all of the correct contact points.
cases.answer: The wire is on the D-cell are on the light bulb.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Georgia found one brown mineral and one black mineral. How will she know which one is harder?
cases.model_answer: The harder mineral will leave a scratch on the less hard mineral. If the black mineral is harder, the brown mineral will have a scratch.
cases.answer: The harder one leave a scratch on the less scratch mineral.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Beth made 2 solutions of different concentrations of water and citric acid. She put 50 milliliters of the first solution in cup X and 50 milliliters of the second solution in cup Y. When she put the cups on the balance, the balance looked as shown below. Which solution, X or Y, is more concentrated? Explain how you know which is more concentrated.
cases.model_answer: X. When equal amounts of 2 solutions are compared, the solution that is more concentrated will have the greater mass (weigh more). 50 milliliters of X has a greater mass than 50 milliliters of Y, so X must be more concentrated.
cases.answer: X, because solution x weighs more and has more solute.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Denise made a circuit to light a bulb or run a motor. She used a special switch. Below is the schematic diagram of her circuit. The switch is inside the dotted box. What will happen when she moves the switch to the left?
cases.model_answer: The bulb will light.
cases.answer: The light bulb will turn on.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Anna wants to compare the fat in walnuts and peanuts, but she isn't sure how. Write a procedure Anna can use to compare the fat in walnuts and peanuts.
cases.model_answer: Measure out equal masses of walnuts and peanuts. Smash the samples uniformly in the same size area on brown paper. Wait the same time for each sample.
cases.answer: First you have to have these materials, 2 brown paper indicators, weigh machine, 2 cups, one gram block, spoon and stick. You put 2 cup on each side of the weigh machine with brown paper on each of the cups. Then you smear the food sample on the brown indicator then wait for 2 day.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Why was the siren's sound designed to have this property?
cases.model_answer: So that people notice the sound.
cases.answer: Because to warn people to get out of the way.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Darla tied one end of a string around a doorknob and held the other end in her hand. When she plucked the string (pulled and let go quickly) she heard a sound. How would the pitch change if Darla made the string longer?
cases.model_answer: When the string is longer, the pitch will be lower.
cases.answer: It would be low pitch.
cases.label: right

cases.question: The motors shown at the right with the D-cell batteries will NOT run. Explain why.
cases.model_answer: The negative terminals of the D-cell batteries are facing each other, so there is no flow of electricity.
cases.answer: They will not run because negative is pointing to negative.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Why does a rubber band make a sound when you pluck it (pull and let go quickly)?
cases.model_answer: The rubber band vibrates.
cases.answer: Because it vibrates.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Mary told her friend Sharice that she had a rug to sell. Sharice asked if the rug would fit perfectly, wall to wall, in her bedroom. Mary went home and measured the rug. She put her feet heel-to-toe and counted the number of shoe lengths it took to measure the rug. She found the rug was 18 shoes long and 12 shoes wide. Sharice did the same thing in her room to measure the space for the rug. Her floor was 18 shoes long and 12 shoes wide. A perfect fit! Sharice bought the rug and took it home. To her dismay, she found it was too short and too narrow for her bedroom! What could Mary and Sharice do to better measure the size of the rug?
cases.model_answer: Use a standard unit of measurement such as centimeters or meters.
cases.answer: They should use a standard.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Draw an arrow to show which direction the water flows in the river. (Rose Mountain is on the left and Happy Valley is on the right in the drawing.) Why do you think the water flows in that direction?
cases.model_answer: Water will always flow downhill (mountain to valley).
cases.answer: Because somewhere in that mountain there is a water source and the water flows down the mountain.
cases.label: right

cases.question: What is your "rule" for deciding if the part of a plant you are observing is a fruit?
cases.model_answer: If a part of the plant contains seeds, that part is the fruit.
cases.answer: If it has seed inside it is a fruit.
cases.label: right

cases.question: Joanne mixed material R and material D together, added water, and stirred. After a few minutes, the liquid was clear and there was a solid on the bottom of the cup. Joanne used a paper filter to separate the solid from the liquid. Why does the solid stay in the filter when the liquid goes through?
cases.model_answer: The particles of the solid are too big to go through the holes in the paper filter.
cases.answer: Because the solid is big and it cannot go through the filter paper.

cases.question: Gerry used a paper filter to separate a mixture of sand, salt, and water. Think about particle size and answer this question: Why did the salt go through the filter while the sand got caught?

cases.question: Don wanted to find out if a battery powered toy truck would always travel the same distance in 10 seconds no matter how heavy a load the truck carried. He placed one or more blocks (the load) in the back of the truck and recorded his results. (Each block had the same mass.) The following graph displays his results. What is the relationship between the number of blocks and the distance traveled by the truck in 10 seconds?

cases.answer: When he had 0 blocks it went 5 meters and when he had 2 it went 3 meters when had 4 it went one meter.

cases.question: Adam's friend gave him a cup filled with a water solution. Adam did not know what solid material was used to make it. He evaporated the solution and found crystals in the dish after all of the water was gone. How will the crystals help him decide what solid material was used to make the solution?

cases.question: Mariella made a saturated solution by adding a solid to 100 milliliters water. Richard made a saturated solution by adding the same solid to 250 milliliters water. Do the 2 saturated solutions have the same concentration? Explain your answer.

cases.answer: No because Mariella's is more concentrated because her's has less water so it is taste more sweeter or saltier.

cases.question: Julie and David each built a solar water heater. Both solar water heaters were 10 centimeters x 10 centimeters x 30 centimeters. They checked the temperatures every 5 minutes and made the table below. Which box did Julie build, A or B? What evidence supports your answer?
cases.model_answer: A. The water in Julie's heater got hotter faster (or had a greater temperature change in 20 minutes). The collector in heater A has the greater surface area so the water in A would get hotter faster than the water in B.
cases.answer: B. That they both painted black on the inside in the bottom and filled the top with liters of water. And the heaters will set the sun.
